title: Add the native unit suite as a path-scoped flow check
description:
Split from ticket dc17c058 (Factory audit follow-up, part 2) on the owner's decision of 2026-11-15. Replaces ticket 724821da, closed because it was created with a wrong parent link.

Add a 'unit' entry to checks in .factory2/config.json next to 'whitespace', proposed as: command 'make -C indigo_test test-unit', paths indigo_libs/*, indigo_server/*, indigo_test/unit/*, indigo_test/test_runner.h, indigo_test/Makefile, timeout_seconds 600. Paths are fnmatch globs and '*' also matches '/'; a check without matching changed files is not selected.

Two prerequisites, both found on 2026-11-15:
1. The unit suite fails on master at test_protocol_security 'device ACL requires device or nonzero master token' (ticket 21bfa946, not linked as a parent on purpose; 50 of 88 suites ran, exit status 2). The check must not be added before that is fixed, or it blocks every ticket touching those paths.
2. A ticket worktree has no Makefile.inc (generated, gitignored, with absolute BUILD_ROOT/BUILD_LIB of the primary checkout) and no built library, so the command fails there immediately. Decide and verify how the check gets a library in a worktree (reuse the primary build or build in the worktree) and measure the cost; in the primary checkout with a built library the suite took about 32 s.

Keep driver, simulator, hardware and shell_compliance tests out of the generic check list, and keep project/commands in .factory2/project-rules.json consistent with the result.

outcome.summary: Pass. Diff limited to .factory2/config.json (new 'unit' check) and the project/commands rule; both valid JSON, config.validate accepts the entry, no other rule changed, no pbxproj change. Configured command is byte-identical to the recorded command-1 (passed at 59a76292e3). Reviewer reran it in the worktree: exit 0 in 61 s warm, 39 suites, 512 PASS, 0 FAIL; worktree status clean afterwards; Makefile.inc BUILD_ROOT/BUILD_LIB/BUILD_DRIVERS point into the worktree. The three archives match the BUILD_DRIVERS dependencies of UNIT_TESTS (platesolver_core, scheduler_*, system_alpaca_json); libprimalucelib is built by test-unit itself, libraw/libindigocat by indigo_libs all. test-unit exits with the failing suite's status. Real fnmatch selection: unit is selected for indigo_libs/, indigo_server/, indigo_test/unit/, test_runner.h, indigo_test/Makefile and not for indigo_docs/, drivers, .factory2/, top-level Makefile or other indigo_test dirs. Timeout 600 s vs 143 s cold / 61 s warm is adequate. Out of scope, for the owner: changes to agent_platesolver/agent_scheduler/system_alpaca, shared/primalucelib, Makefile or Makefile.drv do not select the check although the suite covers or depends on them (matches the approved path list); several unit test rules lack header dependencies, so warm incremental runs after indigo_libs header edits can run stale test binaries; on hosts without make (Windows) a selected unit check cannot pass, which would block closing core tickets there.

history.text: Building worktree library to measure cold unit run
Cold run of configured unit command
Cold run again; unit suite also needs system_alpaca archive
Measuring truly fresh cold run in a scratch git worktree
Running flow check (whitespace) and unit command via --command
Check command-1 started: make Makefile.inc && make init && make -j8 -C indigo_libs all && make -j8 -C indigo_drivers/agent_platesolver -f ../../Makefile.drv all && make -j8 -C

Unit check: command builds from the worktree (make Makefile.inc, make init, indigo_libs, archives agent_platesolver/agent_scheduler/system_alpaca, then test-unit); only those 3 driver archives are needed by UNIT_TESTS (not 104). Measured in a fresh scratch git worktree: cold 143 s, warm 58 s (512 PASS); timeout 600 s. Failure propagation: a broken md5 assertion made the command exit 2. Paths select the check for indigo_libs/indigo_server/indigo_test/unit/test_runner.h/indigo_test/Makefile changes, not for .factory2 or indigo_docs changes. Factory reads config.json from the PRIMARY checkout, so the new check is not selectable by name before merge; it was run via --command with the exact configured command (passed, exit 0, 58 s warm).
Reviewer running the configured unit command once in the worktree
